chapter.title: Opening question
chapter.subtitle: What can I check before I sign?

intro.sub: In this video I walk you through my PhD thesis, step by step.

intro.sub: It starts from one small permission that you give in your wallet.

lines.sub: The title is: Integrating ERC-20 Allowance Edges into PageRank for Enhanced On-Chain Wallet Reputation Scoring.

lines.sub: I am Taehong Kwon.

lines.sub: My supervisor is Professor Mnkandla, and my co-supervisors are Professor Moulla and Dr. Attipoe.

lines.sub: This is the main question of the thesis.

lines.sub: What do ERC-20 allowance edges add to PageRank?
lines.tts: What do E R C twenty allowance edges add to PageRank?

lines.sub: We ask this for one use: PageRank as a reputation score for smart contracts on Arbitrum One.
lines.tts: We ask this for one use, PageRank as a reputation score for smart contracts on Arbitrum One.

lines.sub: A smart contract is simply a program that runs on a blockchain.
lines.tts: A smart contract is simply a program that runs on a blockchain.

lines.sub: I compare against two things.
lines.tts: I compare against two things.

lines.sub: One is AWP, the existing score that walks over the transfer records.
lines.tts: One is A W P, the existing score that walks over the transfer records.

lines.sub: AWP stands for Adaptive Weighted PageRank. A PageRank score comes from a walker hopping along the edges, which I build up in chapter 4.
lines.tts: A W P stands for Adaptive Weighted PageRank. A PageRank score comes from a walker hopping along the edges, which I build up in chapter four.

lines.sub: The other is the plain count of edges, called the raw degree. Both walks start from these counts and smooth them out.
lines.tts: The other is the plain count of edges, called the raw degree. Both walks start from these counts and smooth them out.

card.title: Raw degree
card.body: The plain count of a contract's edges, with no walk at all

lines.sub: In this thesis, the score that walks over the allowances is called EndorseRank.
lines.tts: In this thesis, the score that walks over the allowances is called EndorseRank.

lines.sub: I split the main question into five research questions, listed on the right.
lines.tts: I split the main question into five research questions, listed on the right.

lines.sub: The first three ask whether the two scores order contracts differently, how closely each agrees with the checks I define later, and what each costs to compute.

lines.sub: The first real test is RQ4. Do the scores predict what happens later, and do they predict it better than the raw degree?

lines.sub: The second is RQ5, which mixes the two kinds of edges.
